_readme: Every legal figure of the site lives here (RECETTE §4, §22). Each value was read on the official page cited in `sources` on retrieved_at. Annual update: thresholds on 1 July (ATO page updated in June), rebate percentages on 1 April (Department of Health circular in February or March), premiums monthly (data.gov.au release of the 1st, scripts/data/build-premiums.py).

mls._note: ATO, Medicare levy surcharge income, thresholds and rates (last updated 22 June 2026) and M2 instructions 2026. Tier boundaries are inclusive ('$105,000 or less'). The family thresholds rise by $1,500 for each MLS dependent child after the first. The rate is applied to taxable income + reportable fringe benefits + amounts on which family trust distribution tax was paid, not to the whole income for MLS purposes.

spouseOwnIncomeFloor._note: M2 instructions 2026 (last updated 30 May 2026): with a spouse for the whole year and a combined income above the family threshold, you are not liable if your own income for MLS purposes is $28,011 or less. The ATO page 'Paying the Medicare levy surcharge' (5 May 2026) still prints $27,222. No 2026-27 figure was published on 2026-10-19.

rebate._note: ATO, Income thresholds and rates for the private health insurance rebate (last updated 22 June 2026); privatehealth.gov.au rebate page; Department of Health circular PHI 12/26 (17 February 2026): RAF 2026 = 0.993, industry weighted average premium increase 4.41 %. Rows: under 65, 65 to 69, 70 and over (age of the oldest person on the policy). Columns: base tier, tier 1, tier 2, tier 3. The income tiers are those of the MLS.

proposal2027._note: Department of Health, 'Modernising the Private Health Insurance Rebate' (July 2026): from 1 April 2027 the 65-69 and 70+ rows would take the under-65 rates, subject to legislation passing Parliament; RAF set to 1 for 1 April 2027. Bill: Private Health Insurance Amendment (Modernising the Private Health Insurance Rebate) Bill 2026 [No. 2], introduced in the House of Representatives on 15 October 2026, status 'Before House of Representatives' on aph.gov.au, read 2026-10-19. Not law.

lhc._note: privatehealth.gov.au, Lifetime Health Cover; ATO, Lifetime health cover loading (5 May 2026). Loading = 2 % for every year over 30, based on age on the 1 July before joining; maximum 70 %; removed after 10 years of continuous hospital cover; 1094 days of absence allowed in a lifetime; overseas visits of up to 90 consecutive days keep you overseas; born on or before 1 July 1934 exempt; couple policy: average of the two adults; no rebate on the loading.

ageDiscount._note: privatehealth.gov.au, Age-based discount: insurers may offer 2 % per year under 30, up to 10 % for 18 to 25, kept until 41, then reduced by 2 % a year. Optional for the insurer.

medicareLevy._note: privatehealth.gov.au MLS page: the surcharge is in addition to the Medicare levy of 2 %. ATO Medicare levy reduction (30 June 2026): 2025-26 single low-income thresholds $28,011 and $35,013 (SAPTO $44,268 and $55,335).

dependants._note: ATO, Family and dependants for MLS purposes (21 August 2026): a child is an MLS dependant under 21, or 21 to 24 and studying full time; spouse married or de facto; a foster child is not included; the private health insurance dependant age (up to 31 under the 2021 rules) is a separate notion.
